title: A phishing message that reached people
for: A message asking for credentials, payment or a download, delivered to one or more mailboxes.

steps.title: Get the original message with its headers, not a forward
steps.why: The sender, the links and the route are in the headers a forward drops.

steps.title: Search the mail system for every copy
steps.why: One report usually means many deliveries.

steps.title: Remove the message from every mailbox it reached
steps.why: The person who has not opened it yet still can.
steps.undo: Restore the message from quarantine if it turns out to be legitimate.

steps.title: Block the sender, the links and any attachment digest, and add them as indicators
steps.why: The next wave reuses them, and adding them looks back through what is already stored.
steps.undo: Remove the block and the indicators if they turn out to be legitimate.

steps.title: Find who followed the link or opened the attachment, from proxy, DNS or mail logs
steps.why: Receiving it is not the incident; acting on it is.

steps.title: Ask those people whether they entered a password or approved a prompt
steps.why: Logs show the visit and not what was typed.

steps.title: Open the account playbook for anybody who did
steps.why: From here it is an account somebody else may be using.

steps.title: Tell the people who received it what it was
steps.why: They will otherwise keep wondering whether to click.
